summary: Call focused on what Redwood captures in audit & admin telemetry, export paths (syslog, S3, webhook), retention options and encryption/KMS patterns. Customer wanted assurance on sensitive fields, BYOK (customer-managed keys), SSO/RBAC event capture and evidence for SOC 2/ISO audits. Agreed next steps: share SOC2 artifacts, provide audit export samples, and run a pilot ingestion to Oxbridge SIEM.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We have about 45 minutes, wanted to walk through audit telemetry and answer any compliance questions.
[00:00:15] Lydia Park (CISO): Thanks Ava. We're mainly interested in admin activity — who changed RBAC roles, SSO provisioning, key rotations, plus export options for our SIEM. Also need to understand default retention and the ability to apply legal holds.
[00:00:30] Ava Chen: Totally. Diego will walk through the actual event model and exports. Diego?
[00:00:35] Diego Morales (SE): Cool. Quick context: Redwood captures three broad buckets - control-plane admin events, data-plane inference events (we can opt out for PII), and system health telemetry. For compliance you care about admin events — user create/delete, role changes, API key operations, model rollout changes, canary/rollback events, KMS key usage logs, and console logins.
[00:00:55] Marcus Lee (VP Eng): When you say KMS key usage logs, do you capture the key material? We need to keep keys in HSM and not have key material leave our control.
[00:01:05] Diego Morales (SE): No key material is ever stored. We record metadata about KMS operations — key id, operation (encrypt/decrypt/sign), timestamp, principal. If using Redwood-managed KMS we log calls; with BYOK (customer-managed key) in a customer cloud, the key never goes into Redwood. We can annotate audit events with the key arn but not the secret.
[00:01:25] Tara Singh (Cloud Security): We need KMS logs fed into our own KMS and to our central audit set. Does Redwood support forwarding to our syslog or S3?
[00:01:33] Diego Morales (SE): Yes — three supported export sinks today: push to your S3 bucket (s3://...), streaming syslog over TLS, and a webhook that posts JSON events. We also support batching for large volumes. For Splunk/Elastic we recommend S3+Ingest or syslog depending on throughput.
[00:01:50] Ben Carter (Platform): What's the schema? Are user ids normalized to our identity provider? We use SAML + SCIM for provisioning.
[00:01:58] Diego Morales (SE): We include both Redwood-internal subject id and federated id when available. If SCIM is set up, events contain scim_id, email, and role_name. There are edge cases where email may be proxied or obfuscated, transcription might show 'scim' as 'skim' in earlier docs — sorry if docs are messy. We'll send a clear mapping file.
[00:02:20] Lydia Park (CISO): Good. For SOC 2 evidence, auditors want immutable audit trails and SHA hashes. How do you guarantee immutability?
[00:02:30] Diego Morales (SE): Our hosted offering writes audit events to an append-only store with retention policies and integrates with object stores for long-term archival. Events are write-once; we can provide export snapshots and a signed hash chain for a time window if needed for audits. For Private/VPC deployments customers can mount their own object store to get full control.
[00:02:50] Priya Rao (Compliance): Is there an option to disable retention deletion? Legal needs ability to put a hold on records while investigations are open.
[00:02:58] Ava Chen: Yes, we support legal hold flags — when a hold is applied for an account or scope we prevent deletion for that scope until the hold is released. Diego, quick note on retention defaults?
[00:03:08] Diego Morales (SE): Default retention for audit logs in hosted tier is 90 days; you can extend to 1, 3, 7 years for an additional retention fee. For Dedicated and Private customers we support customizable retention down to your region and export TTLs. Also note long-term archival is encrypted and can be configured to use customer-managed keys.
[00:03:27] Marcus Lee (VP Eng): Pricing impact on long retention? Ballpark?
[00:03:31] Ava Chen: We'll send a pricing sheet. Typically retention is priced by GB-month; long tails add incremental storage. We'll include estimates based on your traffic.
[00:03:40] Tara Singh (Cloud Security): Regarding PII, can you redact sensitive fields at ingestion? We don't want raw prompt text leaving our VPC for some workloads.
[00:03:48] Diego Morales (SE): We have configurable redaction rules — token-level masking, regex-based field stripping, and a redact-on-export mode. For private deployments you can opt to never send prompt text to Redwood control plane; Redwood can capture only metadata (token counts, latency) and keep payloads local. There's also an option to hash or truncate prompts before export.
[00:04:12] Lydia Park (CISO): For SSO events, do you capture failed logins, MFA challenges, session invalidations?
[00:04:18] Diego Morales (SE): Yes, auth events include successful and failed logins, MFA challenge/pass/fail, session creation and revocation, token refresh events, and SCIM provisioning actions. We also log OAuth client changes if you use API clients.
[00:04:33] Ben Carter (Platform): How about admin actions inside Redwood Console — are console clicks recorded? We need evidence of who changed feature flags and rollout policies.
[00:04:41] Diego Morales (SE): We capture console actions as admin events with UI context for the operation (route, resource_id, before/after snapshot where appropriate). For sensitive fields we only record diffs, never plaintext secrets.
[00:04:55] Speaker 1: Could you do a quick layout of an export? Like a five-line example?
[00:05:00] Diego Morales (SE): Sure. Example syslog payload — timestamp, event_type, principal_email, principal_id, resource_type, resource_id, action, outcome, ip, user_agent, metadata. We'll attach a sample file.
[00:05:12] Marcus Lee (VP Eng): Any latency concerns on exporting? We need near-real-time for security monitoring.
[00:05:18] Diego Morales (SE): Syslog can be streamed with sub-second to low-second latency depending on network. Webhook is near-real-time with retries and backoff. S3 is batched — generally minute-level. We'll recommend syslog for SOC teams that need streaming.
[00:05:33] Ava Chen: On encryption — customer-managed KMS, rotation, and attestation — Lydia asked about HSM-level assurance.
[00:05:41] Diego Morales (SE): We support BYOK with external KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). You can bring keys that are HSM-backed. Key rotation is handled by the KMS; Redwood logs the rotation events. For attestation, we can provide KMS audit logs and linkage into the event stream.
[00:05:59] Lydia Park (CISO): For SOC2, ISO evidence, will you provide a mapping matrix — which logs correspond to which control?
[00:06:06] Ava Chen: Yes — we'll share a controls-to-evidence matrix that maps Redwood events to common SOC2 and ISO controls.
[00:06:12] Priya Rao (Compliance): Can we get redacted example exports showing PII removed?
[00:06:16] Diego Morales (SE): Absolutely — that's in the action items. We'll create a redacted sample and a non-redacted one for your private environment.
[00:06:23] Ben Carter (Platform): Who has access to raw audit logs internally at Redwood? We need least privilege and break-glass procedures documented.
[00:06:30] Diego Morales (SE): Internally we have RBAC for access to audit streams. Only a small SRE/infra team has access and all their access is logged and subject to break-glass, with approvals and time-limited tokens. We can provide an access list and the break-glass workflow for auditors.
[00:06:45] Lydia Park (CISO): Data residency — we need logs to remain in EU for EU customers. Does Redwood support region-scoped retention?
[00:06:52] Diego Morales (SE): Yes. Hosted customers can pick region for storage; Dedicated and Private obviously can be deployed in-region or on-prem. Exports to your S3 in region keep data in-region. We'll document the region mapping for audit.
[00:07:05] Marcus Lee (VP Eng): Is there downstream correlation id support so we can join inference traces to audit events?
[00:07:11] Diego Morales (SE): We include request_id and trace_id fields in events so you can correlate tokens, latency traces, and admin actions. If you pass through your own correlation id we preserve it.
[00:07:22] Tara Singh (Cloud Security): Are there built-in alerting rules for suspicious admin activity like mass role grants?
[00:07:28] Diego Morales (SE): We have baseline anomaly detectors in Console and can push those events to your SIEM. For large customers we recommend implementing rules in your SIEM with the exported fields. We can provide example Sigma rules.
[00:07:40] Ava Chen: Quick recap — we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, a sample export (syslog + s3), retention/pricing doc, and schedule a pilot ingestion. Any final questions?
[00:07:52] Lydia Park (CISO): One more — legal hold audit: can you provide an immutable snapshot with signed hash for the horizon of an investigation?
[00:07:59] Diego Morales (SE): Yes, we can produce an immutable snapshot and a signed hash chain for a bounded time window; for long investigations we'd recommend exporting to your own archival store where you control immutability.
[00:08:10] Priya Rao (Compliance): Good. Thanks.
[00:08:14] Ava Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with all the artifacts and propose dates for the pilot.
[00:08:20] [call ended]
